title: Tips + Starter Prompt to improve your game's efficiency
author: fapfap_ahh
selftext:
Part of "polishing" work I feel is reducing any hitches in game play. Doing a bit of research and analysis of my game's frame data, I saw that I was definitely generating and then garbage collecting many more instances than needed per frame. 

So I did some digging on Unity docs, worked with Claude to come up with a script+tools, and then iterated over a few times to nail my targets on my mid tier setup (4K, Max Graphics, 60fps, low 1%'s)

There's a starter prompt at the bottom for anyone who needs it :)

Unity's docs: reduce frequent managed allocations "ideally to 0 bytes per frame, or as close to zero as you can get." ([Unity Manual: Garbage collector overview](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/performance-garbage-collector.html))

**Some numbers** (station, headless, 2,000 frames):

* Per-frame garbage improvement: **\~2.5 KB → \~0.06 KB** (about 97% less). Unity's example: 1 KB a frame at 60 fps = 60 KB/s. We're at \~4 KB/s.\* Radar screen painter: \~0.6 ms a frame with 3.4 ms spikes → **\~0.06 ms**

**Tools:**

* A headless profile run: plays the game in batch mode and records a capture
* A capture analyzer that reads `.raw` files without opening the Profiler window: slowest frames with their hot path, own time per marker, garbage per frame by who made it
* A "deep" mode that names the exact method behind each allocation
* GPU render diags and a quality-tier sweep for the graphics side
* A guard test that fails if steady play starts allocating again

**Starter prompt** if you want to build your own:

>Write a Unity editor script that loads a Profiler `.raw` capture in batch mode (ProfilerDriver.LoadProfile + GetRawFrameDataView) and prints the 15 slowest frames and the top managed allocations per frame, grouped by the marker that made them. Then add a PlayMode test that plays my main scene for 20 seconds while recording to a `.raw`, so I can profile without opening the editor.
